insights.title: Failed payments crossed threshold
insights.summary: Failed-payment rate is 5.0% across 1514 invoice attempts.
insights.recommendation: Check billing provider status, card decline reasons, and plan concentration.
insights.message: Stripe alert (high, score 95): failed-payment rate hit 5.0% (76 failures / 1,505 invoice attempts), crossing the threshold. This matters because elevated payment failures can directly suppress realized revenue and distort retention metrics. Next to inspect: Stripe/billing provider status during the window, the specific card decline reasons driving the 76 failures, and whether failures are concentrated in particular plans (plan concentration).

insights.title: Revenue source outperforming baseline
insights.summary: Meta Ads new MRR is up 500.0% vs the recent baseline.
insights.recommendation: Inspect the winning campaign, segment, and landing path for repeatable patterns.
insights.message: Meta Ads is outperforming baseline: new MRR is $990 vs $792 (+25%), with 10 paid vs 8 baseline. insights.title: Revenue source outperforming baseline
insights.summary: Organic new MRR is up 62.6% vs the recent baseline.
insights.recommendation: Inspect the winning campaign, segment, and landing path for repeatable patterns.
insights.message: Organic is outperforming baseline: new MRR is $1,741 today vs $1,210 baseline (+43.9%), with paid conversions flat (9 today vs 9 baseline). This suggests the lift is coming from higher MRR per conversion or larger deals rather than more paid volume. Next, inspect what changed within Organic: the specific campaign/source detail, audience segment, and landing path driving the higher MRR, plus whether the uplift is concentrated in a few accounts or broad-based.

insights.title: Revenue source outperforming baseline

insights.recommendation: Inspect the winning campaign, segment, and landing path for repeatable patterns.
insights.message: Referral is outperforming baseline: new MRR is $529 today vs $397 baseline (+33.2%; score 76.64, medium). Paid conversions also increased (11 today vs 3 baseline), suggesting the lift is translating into more paying customers, not just higher ARPA. Next to inspect: which specific referral campaign/partner drove the gain, which segments converted, and the landing path users followed before paying (to find repeatable patterns).

insights.title: Revenue source outperforming baseline
insights.summary: Google Ads new MRR is up 27.5% vs the recent baseline.
insights.recommendation: Inspect the winning campaign, segment, and landing path for repeatable patterns.
insights.message: Google Ads is outperforming baseline on revenue: new MRR is $1,782 today vs $1,420 baseline (+25.5%, severity: medium). This matters because revenue rose despite fewer paid conversions (8 today vs 10 baseline), implying higher MRR per paid signup or a shift toward higher-value customers. Next to inspect: which specific campaign/ad group/keyword segment drove the lift, and the landing path tied to those signups to identify repeatable patterns.
